chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abī Maryam, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “No hadd punishment is to be carried out upon anyone in the land of the enemy.”

key_terms.أَرْضِ الْعَدُوِّ: The territory or land of the enemy
key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.حَدٌّ: A prescribed legal punishment in Islamic law

ai.seo_question: Can a hadd punishment be carried out in enemy territory according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام that a hadd punishment is not to be enforced in enemy territory. It reflects jurisprudential concern for proper legal authority, circumstances, and the administration of penalties.
